newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR, AZHARUDDIN LIFT INDIA WITH RECORD STAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR, AZHARUDDIN LIFT INDIA WITH RECORD STAND.

text.p: Sachin Tendulkar and Mohammad Azharuddin lifted India's morale with a record partnership on the third day of the second test against South Africa on Saturday.
The pair put on 222 off only 244 balls -- a record sixth wicket stand by any country against South Africa -- to rescue India after they had plunged to 58 for five during the morning session.
Although they were parted on 280, 50 short of the total needed to avoid the follow-on, Tendulkar watchfully saw his side to the relative safety of 359 before he was last man out for 169.
South Africa lost two quick wickets before the close but, at 24 for two, held a 194-run lead.
India lost the first match of three-test series by 328 runs in Durban and must avoid defeat in Cape Town to keep the series alive.

Those hopes looked distant as Saurav Ganguly and V.V.S Laxman both fell to catches behind the wicket in the first eight overs of the day as India lurched from their overnight 29 for three to 58 for five.

Tendulkar was joined by Azharuddin and, although they had their sticky moments against the home pace attack, they averted immediate disaster by seeing their side to 145 for five at lunch, with Tendulkar racing to 72.
After lunch Azharuddin took over, launching a furious assault as India put on 100 in the first hour after the interval with Tendulkar, who was 46 ahead of his partner at the break, caught in the 80s.
Both enjoyed good fortune. Azharuddin was dropped on 55 and 68 and Tendulkar was put down on 80 and 154.
Azharuddin was particularly severe on Lance Klusener, whose 12 overs cost 88.

Tendulkar won a close race to three figures -- his 11th test century -- with Azharuddin posting his third hundred in the last four tests against South Africa shortly afterwards from only 96 balls with 16 fours and a straight six off Paul Adams.

Their partnership had eclipsed the highest sixth wicket stand against South Africa of 206 by England's Ken Barrington and Jim Parks at Durban in 1964-65 when Azharuddin was run out attempting an impossible single to backward point.
Nayan Mongia was lbw to Adams's chinaman and Allan Donald dismissed Anil Kumble with his third delivery with the second new ball to make it 315 for eight with India still 15 runs short of safety.
But Javagal Srinath partnered Tendulkar to safety before falling to Shaun Pollock. Adam Bacher took a leaping one-handed catch on the square leg boundary to dismiss Tendulkar.
His 169 came from 331 balls and included 26 fours.
